sentences.text: Gongshuilong is distinguished by exceptionally long and curved neural spines on its tail vertebrae that created a tall, sail-like structure.
These spines measured about 8.5 times the height of the vertebral centra, the central part of each vertebra, and curved slightly backward.
The sail-like tail makes Gongshuilong the first hadrosaurid from South China known to possess such a structure.
Its name, fanwei, directly references this prominent sail.
Fossils were uncovered in March 2021 during construction work in Shahe, near Ganzhou in Jiangxi Province, China.
Han Yao and colleagues formally described the new genus and species in 2026.
The only known species, G. fanwei, is represented by a bonebed that includes at least two individuals, suggesting they may have lived or died together.
Phylogenetic analysis places Gongshuilong within the tribe Brachylophosaurini of the Saurolophinae clade.
It inhabited what is now China during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
The precise relationships among members of Brachylophosaurini remain uncertain, with Gongshuilong forming a polytomy alongside Wulagasaurus, Acristavus, and other North American taxa.
